title: Adaptive per-tenant inflight limiter and edge hedge to prevent 5xx/timeouts during escalations
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: High-severity customer escalations over the past week traced to a compound failure mode: long-context requests cause kernel-selection and KV-cache thrash in the serving runtime producing long tail latencies and occasional OOMs; SDKs with aggressive retry settings amplify load leading to proxy/backpressure exhaustion and 502/503s for multiple tenants. This ticket implements a runtime+edge control to limit inflight load per tenant adaptively and a fast-path hedge to a compatible model variant to keep customer requests healthy during spikes.
impact_summary: Several enterprise customers experienced repeated 5xx and timeouts during peak jobs and migrations. Customer support escalations led to manual throttles and temporary reserved capacity allocation. Business impact: degraded SLA for 3 customers, increased on-call load, and lost confidence in hosted stability for long-sequence workloads.
root_cause_summary: Not a simple retry-loop bug. Root cause was twofold: 1) kernel selection and KV cache compaction for >8k context lengths triggers multiple slow fallbacks that push individual request latency into the tail and occasionally cause memory pressure; 2) client-side SDKs retry aggressively (4x backoff misconfiguration) without honoring partial response semantics, producing synchronous retry waves. Combined these create sudden inflight spikes the edge/proxy can't shed quickly, leading to 502/503 cascades.
steps_taken: Collected p50/p95/p999 traces for affected tenants (Grafana link) and correlated with kernel-selection timing across runtime hosts
Temporarily applied per-tenant admission caps for the most impacted customers to bring systems back to baseline
Disabled an experimental kernel-fallback path in a targeted pool to validate its contribution to tail latency
Published immediate SDK guidance to customers to reduce retry attempts and enable idempotency tokens where appropriate
Opened this engineering ticket for a durable solution (adaptive limiter + edge hedge) and associated rollout plan
proposed_fix: 1) Implement an adaptive per-tenant inflight limiter inside the frontdoor admission controller that calculates allowed_concurrency = max(2, floor(baseline_qps * dynamic_factor)) derived from recent p50/p95 latency and error rate. 2) Add an 'edge hedge' fast-fail to a compatible model variant (lower memory, faster kernel) when a tenant's inflight exceeds soft limit and latency breach occurs. 3) Add a tracing + backpressure signal from runtime to edge so the limiter uses host-level memory pressure hints. 4) Add telemetry to measure retry amplification and synthetic canaries to validate correctness.
acceptance_criteria: Deploy limiter and edge-hedge to canary (5% traffic) without increase in 5xxs for canary tenants
p95 tail latency for long-context workloads reduced by >= 30% compared to pre-change baseline for canary tenants
No increase in token/sec cost by more than 5% for controlled tenants
Automated synthetic tests exercise kernel-fallback and confirm edge-hedge triggers as expected
Runbook updated and customer communications template prepared for potential rollbacks
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Unit + integration tests + local perf: branch runtime PR and proxy PR (CI passing required)
Phase 1 (Canary): Deploy to 5% of hosted traffic (low-risk tenants first) for 48 hours; monitor p95, p999, 5xx, and retry amplification metric
Phase 2 (Gradual): 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 24-48 hour observation windows and automatic rollback triggers if >2x increase in 5xx or sustained p999 increase >25%
Rollback plan: Toggle kill-switch at edge-proxy (feature flag) and revert runtime admission config via canary-control plane within 5 minutes
Customer comms: Notify impacted customers (pre-approved template) at start of Phase 1 and after safe completion of Phase 2
notes: This approach intentionally avoids hard tenant-wide caps; it prefers adaptive limits driven by observed latency to preserve throughput where runtime is healthy.
Edge hedge selects model variants validated in the model catalog for output compatibility; devs must add compatibility tests to the model onboarding checklist.
We must coordinate with Dedicated/Private teams to ensure the same limiter config is available for private control planes. That work is tracked separately.
Potential follow-ups: more granular SDK backoff guidance, idempotency enforcement, and a runtime memory-protection shim to prevent OOM-triggered 5xxs
